summary.headline: The Tricentennial Committee advanced plans for 2027 anniversary events, including library programs, drone shows, a firefighters bonfire, and commemorative merchandise.
summary.summary: The Tricentennial Committee reviewed progress across its subcommittees and working groups for the town 300th anniversary celebration in 2027. Library Director Ryan Donovan confirmed funding for a local cemetery history lecture and discussed a possible revival of the Strawberry Social. The committee also discussed an AI-driven Southborough history musical presentation, utility pole banner placements, drone show scheduling, logistics for a firefighters union-sponsored bonfire, and the expanding sales of Tricentennial t-shirts and commemorative bricks.

topics.title: Library collaboration and history talks
topics.summary: Library Director Ryan Donovan presented ideas for tricentennial-themed library programs. He reported that the Friends of the Library agreed to fully fund a $750 tailored gravestone history lecture by the Gravestone Girls, tentatively planned for March 2027. The committee and library director also discussed logistics, volunteer needs, and ticketing for potentially reviving the historic Strawberry Social in June 2027, as well as holding history-related photography exhibits.
key_details: Friends of the Library will fund the $750 Gravestone Girls tailored presentation.
Gravestone lecture tentatively eyed for March 2027 to avoid overlapping with fall cemetery reenactments.
Revival of the Strawberry Social discussed for June 2027, with concerns noted about large crowd size and volunteer needs.
History in Bloom confirmed for April 15-17.
topics.outcome: The library director and committee will continue coordinating programming schedules and logistics.

topics.title: AI musical history project proposal
topics.summary: Resident presenter Sam pitched a 20-chapter, 70-minute AI-generated musical history of Southborough covering key town figures and historical events. Committee members discussed using excerpts as audio branding, website teasers, or background audio at town buildings, but stressed the need to fact-check the AI-generated lyrics and include disclaimers regarding historical accuracy.
key_details: Project contains 20 musical chapters covering town history, Burnett family, Cordaville, and schools.
Members recommended fact-checking the material with local historians before wide distribution.
Presenter suggested involving high school or vocational students to edit and integrate audio clips.
Audio could be featured at senior center kiosks or linked on the tricentennial website.
topics.outcome: Presenter will provide text transcripts and summary sheets for committee review and fact-checking.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved the meeting minutes from June 10 with a minor correction on line 37 and adjourned the meeting.
key_details: June 10 meeting minutes approved with one abstention.
Next meeting scheduled for August 12.

topics.title: Utility pole banners and National Grid coordination
topics.summary: The committee reviewed progress on securing permits to hang anniversary banners from utility poles across Southborough. An initial list of 85 poles was submitted to the town administrator, and volunteers are needed to photograph and document pole numbers across town streets before National Grid and Verizon can grant final approvals.
key_details: 85 utility poles identified along Central Street, Main Street, Southville Road, and near schools.
Each utility pole must be photographed with its visible pole number for application submission.
A volunteer was identified to assist the committee with photography.
topics.outcome: Committee members will coordinate pole photography and compile the application packet for utility companies.

topics.title: Event updates and subcommittees
topics.summary: Working groups reported on multiple anniversary events. The Voices from the Grave cemetery reenactment selected eight historic characters and is actively recruiting actors, particularly men. Andrew confirmed Southborough is booked on the drone company calendar for January 1 and 2, with contract negotiations continuing, while the parade group prepared contracts and participation standards for marching units.
key_details: Voices from the Grave reenactment is researching sermons of Nathan Stone and seeking male actors.
Drone show confirmed on vendor calendar for January 1-2, pending finalized contract and deposit.
Fireman Muster working group requested to officially add Antique to event title and discussed food truck permits.
Oxen owners for the parade deferred formal commitment until early 2027 due to livestock management uncertainties.
House tour working group plans to feature approximately 12 homes, with an update expected in September.
topics.outcome: Working groups will continue planning and report back at future meetings.

topics.title: Tricentennial bonfire and hayride logistics
topics.summary: The chair reported that the Southborough Firefighters Union offered to sponsor, organize, and manage the planned tricentennial bonfire. Members supported pairing the bonfire with either the drone show weekend in January or a December lighting event rather than hosting it as a standalone event. The committee also discussed using a local historic hay wagon for heritage events.
key_details: Southborough Firefighters Union agreed to organize and operate the bonfire event.
Committee favored linking the bonfire to an existing celebration such as First Day or winter light festivals.
A historic hay wagon stored in Southborough is intact and could serve as an attraction or shuttle at Heritage Day.
topics.outcome: The chair will continue discussions with fire department leadership on dates and locations.

topics.title: Fundraising, merchandise, and publicity
topics.summary: The committee reviewed outreach, fundraising, and merchandise operations. Claire Reynolds was recruited to coordinate the commemorative brick campaign database and orders. Tricentennial t-shirts sold out of large and extra-large sizes at the senior center at $20 each, prompting a reorder of 78 shirts, and the committee explored launching an online store for polo shirts and other branded items.
key_details: Claire Reynolds recruited to lead order processing for commemorative bricks.
Reorder of 78 adult t-shirts placed after initial large and XL sizes sold out.
Committee email newsletter has grown to roughly 500 subscribers.
Official website is live at southborough300.com and southborough300.org.
Mass Cultural Council festival grants are being researched for event funding.
topics.outcome: Committee will pursue online store vendor options and continue brick and t-shirt sales.
